celebration.title: Pretiosissimi Sanguinis Domini Nostri Jesu Christi

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, lábia + mea apéries.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, + open thou my lips.

segments.t: Dómine, lábia + mea apéries.

content.latin: ℟. Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

segments.t: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Christum Dei Fílium, qui suo nos redémit sánguine, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Christ, the Son of God, hath redeemed us by His Own Blood, * O come, let us worship Him.

segments.t: Ant.
Christum Dei Fílium, qui suo nos redémit sánguine, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Ant. Christum Dei Fílium, qui suo nos redémit sánguine, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Christ, the Son of God, hath redeemed us by His Own Blood, * O come, let us worship Him.

segments.t: Ant.
Christum Dei Fílium, qui suo nos redémit sánguine, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Christum Dei Fílium, qui suo nos redémit sánguine, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Christ, the Son of God, hath redeemed us by His Own Blood, * O come, let us worship Him.

segments.t: Ant.
Christum Dei Fílium, qui suo nos redémit sánguine, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship Him.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius
(genuflectitur)
veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

content.latin: Ant. Christum Dei Fílium, qui suo nos redémit sánguine, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Christ, the Son of God, hath redeemed us by His Own Blood, * O come, let us worship Him.

segments.t: Ant.
Christum Dei Fílium, qui suo nos redémit sánguine, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship Him.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Ant. Christum Dei Fílium, qui suo nos redémit sánguine, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. Christ, the Son of God, hath redeemed us by His Own Blood, * O come, let us worship Him.

Christum Dei Fílium, qui suo nos redémit sánguine, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Ira iusta Conditóris,
content.english: He who once, in righteous vengeance,

content.latin: Imbre aquárum víndice,
content.english: Whelmed the world beneath the flood,

content.latin: Criminósum mersit orbem
content.english: Once again in mercy cleansed it

content.latin: Noë in arca sóspite:
content.english: With the stream of his own blood,

content.latin: Mira tandem vis amóris
content.english: Coming from his throne on high

content.latin: Lavit orbem sánguine.
content.english: On the painful cross to die.

content.latin: Tam salúbri terra felix
content.english: Blest with this all-saving shower,

content.latin: Irrigáta plúvia,
content.english: Earth her beauty straight resumed;

content.latin: Ante spinas quæ scatébat,
content.english: In the place of thorns and briars,

content.latin: Germinávit flósculos;
content.english: Myrtles sprang, and roses bloomed:

content.latin: Inque néctaris sapórem
content.english: Bitter wormwood of the waste

content.latin: Transiére absýnthia.
content.english: Into honey changed its taste.

content.latin: Triste prótinus venénum
content.english: Scorpions ceased; the slimy serpent

content.latin: Dirus anguis pósuit,
content.english: Laid his deadly poison by;

content.latin: Et cruénta belluárum
content.english: Savage beasts of cruel instinct

content.latin: Désiit ferócia:
content.english: Lost their wild ferocity;

content.latin: Mitis Agni vulneráti
content.english: Welcoming the gentle reign

content.latin: Hæc fuit victória.
content.english: Of the Lamb for sinners slain.

content.latin: O sciéntiæ supérnæ
content.english: Oh, the wisdom of th' eternal!

segments.t: O
sciéntiæ supérnæ

content.latin: Altitúdo impérvia!
content.english: Oh, its depth and height divine!

content.latin: O suávitas benígni
content.english: Oh, the sweetness of that mercy

content.latin: Prædicánda péctoris!
content.english: Which in Jesus Christ doth shine!

content.latin: Servus erat morte dignus,
content.english: Slaves we were condemned to die!

content.latin: Rex luit pœnam óptimus.
content.english: Our King pays the penalty!

content.latin: Quando culpis provocámus
content.english: When before the Judge we tremble,

content.latin: Ultiónem iúdicis,
content.english: Conscious of his broken laws,

content.latin: Tunc loquéntis protegámur
content.english: May this blood, in that dread hour,

content.latin: Sánguinis præséntia;
content.english: Cry aloud, and plead our cause;

content.latin: Ingruéntium malórum
content.english: Bid our guilty terrors cease,

content.latin: Tunc recédant ágmina.
content.english: Be our pardon and our peace.

content.latin: Te redémptus laudet orbis
content.english: Prince and author of salvation!

content.latin: Grata servans múnera,
content.english: Lord of majesty supreme!

content.latin: O salútis sempitérnæ
content.english: Jesu, praise to thee be given

content.latin: Dux et Auctor ínclite,
content.english: By the world thou didst redeem;

content.latin: Qui tenes beáta regna
content.english: Who with the Father and the Spirit,

content.latin: Cum Parénte et Spíritu.
content.english: Reignest in eternal merit.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Nocturnus I
content.english: Nocturn I

segments.t: Nocturnus I

content.latin: Ant. Postquam consummáti sunt * dies octo, ut circumciderétur Puer, vocátum est nomen eius Iesus.
content.english: Ant. And when eight days were accomplished * for the circumcising of the child, His Name was called Jesus.

segments.t: Ant.
Postquam consummáti sunt * dies octo, ut circumciderétur Puer, vocátum est nomen eius Iesus.

content.latin: Psalmus 2 [1]
content.english: Psalm 2 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 2

content.latin: 2:1 Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
content.english: 2:1 Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?

segments.t: Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?

content.latin: 2:2 Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.
content.english: 2:2 The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.

segments.t: Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.

content.latin: 2:3 Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.
content.english: 2:3 Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.

segments.t: Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.

content.latin: 2:4 Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
content.english: 2:4 He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.

segments.t: Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.

content.latin: 2:5 Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
content.english: 2:5 Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.

segments.t: Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.

content.latin: 2:6 Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.
content.english: 2:6 But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.

segments.t: Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.

content.latin: 2:7 Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
content.english: 2:7 The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

segments.t: Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.

content.latin: 2:8 Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
content.english: 2:8 Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

segments.t: Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.

content.latin: 2:9 Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
content.english: 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

segments.t: Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.

content.latin: 2:10 Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.
content.english: 2:10 And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

segments.t: Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.

content.latin: 2:11 Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
content.english: 2:11 Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.

segments.t: Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.

content.latin: 2:12 Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.
content.english: 2:12 Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.

segments.t: Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.

content.latin: 2:13 Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
content.english: 2:13 When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.

segments.t: Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Postquam consummáti sunt dies octo, ut circumciderétur Puer, vocátum est nomen eius Iesus.
content.english: Ant. And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, His Name was called Jesus.

segments.t: Ant.
Postquam consummáti sunt dies octo, ut circumciderétur Puer, vocátum est nomen eius Iesus.

content.latin: Ant. Factus in agonía * prolíxius orábat, et factus est sudor eius sicut guttæ sánguinis decurréntis in terram.
content.english: Ant. And being in an agony * He prayed more earnestly, and His Sweat was as it were great drops of Blood falling down to the ground.

segments.t: Ant.
Factus in agonía * prolíxius orábat, et factus est sudor eius sicut guttæ sánguinis decurréntis in terram.

content.latin: Psalmus 3 [2]
content.english: Psalm 3 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 3

content.latin: 3:2 Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
content.english: 3:2 Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.

segments.t: Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.

content.latin: 3:3 Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.
content.english: 3:3 Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.

segments.t: Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.

content.latin: 3:4 Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
content.english: 3:4 But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.

content.latin: 3:5 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
content.english: 3:5 I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.

segments.t: Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.

content.latin: 3:6 Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
content.english: 3:6 I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.

segments.t: Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.

content.latin: 3:7 Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
content.english: 3:7 I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.

segments.t: Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.

content.latin: 3:8 Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
content.english: 3:8 For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.

segments.t: Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.

content.latin: 3:9 Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.
content.english: 3:9 Salvation is of the Lord: * and thy blessing is upon thy people.

segments.t: Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Factus in agonía prolíxius orábat, et factus est sudor eius sicut guttæ sánguinis decurréntis in terram.
content.english: Ant. And being in an agony He prayed more earnestly, and His Sweat was as it were great drops of Blood falling down to the ground.

segments.t: Ant.
Factus in agonía prolíxius orábat, et factus est sudor eius sicut guttæ sánguinis decurréntis in terram.

content.latin: Ant. Iudas, qui eum trádidit, * pœniténtia ductus rétulit trigínta argénteos, dicens: Peccávi tradens sánguinem iustum.
content.english: Ant. Judas, which had betrayed Him, * repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver, saying: I have sinned, in that I have betrayed the innocent Blood.

segments.t: Ant.
Iudas, qui eum trádidit, * pœniténtia ductus rétulit trigínta argénteos, dicens: Peccávi tradens sánguinem iustum.

content.latin: Psalmus 15 [3]
content.english: Psalm 15 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 15

content.latin: 15:1 Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. * Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.
content.english: 15:1 Preserve me, O Lord, for I have put my trust in thee. * I have said to the Lord, thou art my God, for thou hast no need of my goods.

segments.t: Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. * Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.

content.latin: 15:3 Sanctis, qui sunt in terra eius, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.
content.english: 15:3 To the saints, who are in his land, * he hath made wonderful all my desires in them.

segments.t: Sanctis, qui sunt in terra eius, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.

content.latin: 15:4 Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.
content.english: 15:4 Their infirmities were multiplied: * afterwards they made haste.

segments.t: Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.

content.latin: 15:4 Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.
content.english: 15:4 I will not gather together their meetings for blood offerings: * nor will I be mindful of their names by my lips.

segments.t: Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.

content.latin: 15:5 Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.
content.english: 15:5 The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup: * it is thou that wilt restore my inheritance to me.

segments.t: Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.

content.latin: 15:6 Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.
content.english: 15:6 The lines are fallen unto me in goodly places: * for my inheritance is goodly to me.

segments.t: Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.

content.latin: 15:7 Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.
content.english: 15:7 I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding: * moreover my reins also have corrected me even till night.

segments.t: Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.

content.latin: 15:8 Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.
content.english: 15:8 I set the Lord always in my sight: * for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved.

segments.t: Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.

content.latin: 15:9 Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.
content.english: 15:9 Therefore my heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: * moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope.

segments.t: Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.

content.latin: 15:10 Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.
content.english: 15:10 Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; * nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption.

segments.t: Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.

content.latin: 15:11 Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.
content.english: 15:11 Thou hast made known to me the ways of life, thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance: * at thy right hand are delights even to the end.

segments.t: Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Iudas, qui eum trádidit, pœniténtia ductus rétulit trigínta argénteos, dicens: Peccávi tradens sánguinem iustum.
content.english: Ant. Judas, which had betrayed Him, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver, saying: I have sinned, in that I have betrayed the innocent Blood.

segments.t: Ant.
Iudas, qui eum trádidit, pœniténtia ductus rétulit trigínta argénteos, dicens: Peccávi tradens sánguinem iustum.

content.latin: ℣. Redemísti nos, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Lord, Thou hast redeemed us.

segments.t: Redemísti nos, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. In sánguine tuo.
content.english: ℟. By thy Blood.

segments.t: In sánguine tuo.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: De Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Hebrǽos
content.english: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Hebrews

content.latin: 11 Christus assístens póntifex futurórum bonórum, per ámplius et perféctius tabernáculum, non manufáctum, id est, non huius creatiónis:
content.english: 11 But Christ, being come an high priest of the good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hand, that is, not of this creation:

segments.t: Christus assístens póntifex futurórum bonórum, per ámplius et perféctius tabernáculum, non manufáctum, id est, non huius creatiónis:

content.latin: 12 Neque per sánguinem hircórum aut vitulórum, sed per próprium sánguinem introívit semel in Sancta, ætérna redemptióne invénta.
content.english: 12 Neither by the blood of goats, or of calves, but by his own blood, entered once into the holies, having obtained eternal redemption.

segments.t: Neque per sánguinem hircórum aut vitulórum, sed per próprium sánguinem introívit semel in Sancta, ætérna redemptióne invénta.

content.latin: 13 Si enim sanguis hircórum et taurórum, et cinis vítulæ aspérsus inquinátos sanctíficat ad emundatiónem carnis:
content.english: 13 For if the blood of goats and of oxen, and the ashes of an heifer being sprinkled, sanctify such as are defiled, to the cleansing of the flesh:

segments.t: Si enim sanguis hircórum et taurórum, et cinis vítulæ aspérsus inquinátos sanctíficat ad emundatiónem carnis:

content.latin: 14 Quanto magis sanguis Christi, qui per Spíritum Sanctum semetípsum óbtulit immaculátum Deo, emundábit consciéntiam nostram ab opéribus mórtuis, ad serviéndum Deo vivénti?
content.english: 14 How much more shall the blood of Christ, who by the Holy Ghost offered himself unspotted unto God, cleanse our conscience from dead works, to serve the living God?

segments.t: Quanto magis sanguis Christi, qui per Spíritum Sanctum semetípsum óbtulit immaculátum Deo, emundábit consciéntiam nostram ab opéribus mórtuis, ad serviéndum Deo vivénti?

content.latin: 15 Et ídeo novi testaménti mediátor est: ut morte intercedénte, in redemptiónem eárum prævaricatiónum, quæ erant sub prióri testaménto, repromissiónem accípiant qui vocáti sunt ætérnæ hereditátis.
content.english: 15 And therefore he is the mediator of the new testament: that by means of his death, for the redemption of those transgressions, which were under the former testament, they that are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance.

segments.t: Et ídeo novi testaménti mediátor est: ut morte intercedénte, in redemptiónem eárum prævaricatiónum, quæ erant sub prióri testaménto, repromissiónem accípiant qui vocáti sunt ætérnæ hereditátis.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Iesus, ut sanctificáret per suum sánguinem pópulum, extra portam passus est:
content.english: ℟. Jesus also, that He might sanctify the people with His own Blood, suffered without the gate.

segments.t: Iesus, ut sanctificáret per suum sánguinem pópulum, extra portam passus est:

content.latin: * Exeámus ígitur ad eum extra castra, impropérium eius portántes.
content.english: * Let us go forth therefore unto Him without the camp, bearing His reproach.

content.latin: ℣. Nondum enim usque ad sánguinem restitístis advérsus peccátum repugnántes.
content.english: ℣. Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.

segments.t: Nondum enim usque ad sánguinem restitístis advérsus peccátum repugnántes.

content.latin: ℟. Exeámus ígitur ad eum extra castra, impropérium eius portántes.
content.english: ℟. Let us go forth therefore unto Him without the gate, bearing His reproach.

segments.t: Exeámus ígitur ad eum extra castra, impropérium eius portántes.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 16 Ubi enim testaméntum est, mors necésse est intercédat testatóris.
content.english: For where there is a testament, the death of the testator must of necessity come in.

segments.t: Ubi enim testaméntum est, mors necésse est intercédat testatóris.

content.latin: 17 Testaméntum enim in mórtuis confirmátum est: alióquin nondum valet, dum vivit qui testátus est.
content.english: 17 For a testament is of force, after men are dead: otherwise it is as yet of no strength, whilst the testator liveth.

segments.t: Testaméntum enim in mórtuis confirmátum est: alióquin nondum valet, dum vivit qui testátus est.

content.latin: 18 Unde nec primum quidem sine sánguine dedicátum est.
content.english: 18 Whereupon neither was the first indeed dedicated without blood.

segments.t: Unde nec primum quidem sine sánguine dedicátum est.

content.latin: 19 Lecto enim omni mandáto legis a Móyse univérso pópulo, accípiens sánguinem vitulórum et hircórum cum aqua, et lana coccínea, et hyssópo, ipsum quoque librum, et omnem pópulum aspérsit,
content.english: 19 For when every commandment of the law had been read by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, with water, and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,

segments.t: Lecto enim omni mandáto legis a Móyse univérso pópulo, accípiens sánguinem vitulórum et hircórum cum aqua, et lana coccínea, et hyssópo, ipsum quoque librum, et omnem pópulum aspérsit,

content.latin: 20 Dicens: Hic sanguis testaménti, quod mandávit ad vos Deus.
content.english: 20 Saying: This is the blood of the testament, which God hath enjoined unto you.

segments.t: Dicens: Hic sanguis testaménti, quod mandávit ad vos Deus.

content.latin: 21 Etiam tabernáculum et ómnia vasa ministérii sánguine simíliter aspérsit.
content.english: 21 The tabernacle also and all the vessels of the ministry, in like manner, he sprinkled with blood.

segments.t: Etiam tabernáculum et ómnia vasa ministérii sánguine simíliter aspérsit.

content.latin: 22 Et ómnia pene in sánguine secúndum legem mundántur: et sine sánguinis effusióne non fit remíssio.
content.english: 22 And almost all things, according to the law, are cleansed with blood: and without shedding of blood there is no remission.

segments.t: Et ómnia pene in sánguine secúndum legem mundántur: et sine sánguinis effusióne non fit remíssio.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Móyses sumptum sánguinem respérsit in pópulum:
content.english: ℟. Moses took the blood, and sprinkled all the people;

segments.t: Móyses sumptum sánguinem respérsit in pópulum:

content.latin: * Et ait: Hic est sanguis fœ́deris, quod pépigit Dóminus vobíscum.
content.english: * Saying: This is the blood of the Testament which God hath enjoined unto you.

content.latin: ℣. Fide celebrávit Pascha et sánguinis effusióne, ne qui vastábat primitíva, tángeret eos.
content.english: ℣. Through faith he kept the Passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the first-born should touch them.

segments.t: Fide celebrávit Pascha et sánguinis effusióne, ne qui vastábat primitíva, tángeret eos.

content.latin: ℟. Et ait: Hic est sanguis fœ́deris, quod pépigit Dóminus vobíscum.
content.english: ℟. Saying: This is the blood of the Testament which God hath enjoined unto you.

segments.t: Et ait: Hic est sanguis fœ́deris, quod pépigit Dóminus vobíscum.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 19 Habéntes ítaque, fratres, fidúciam in intróitu sanctórum in sánguine Christi,
content.english: 19 Having therefore, brethren, a confidence in the entering into the holies by the blood of Christ;

segments.t: Habéntes ítaque, fratres, fidúciam in intróitu sanctórum in sánguine Christi,

content.latin: 20 Quam initiávit nobis viam novam, et vivéntem per velámen, id est, carnem suam,
content.english: 20 A new and living way which he hath dedicated for us through the veil, that is to say, his flesh,

segments.t: Quam initiávit nobis viam novam, et vivéntem per velámen, id est, carnem suam,

content.latin: 21 Et sacerdótem magnum super domum Dei:
content.english: 21 And a high priest over the house of God:

segments.t: Et sacerdótem magnum super domum Dei:

content.latin: 22 Accedámus cum vero corde in plenitúdine fídei, aspérsi corda a consciéntia mala, et ablúti corpus aqua munda,
content.english: 22 Let us draw near with a true heart in fulness of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with clean water.

segments.t: Accedámus cum vero corde in plenitúdine fídei, aspérsi corda a consciéntia mala, et ablúti corpus aqua munda,

content.latin: 23 Teneámus spei nostræ confessiónem indeclinábilem (fidélis enim est qui repromísit),
content.english: 23 Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering (for he is faithful that hath promised),

segments.t: Teneámus spei nostræ confessiónem indeclinábilem (fidélis enim est qui repromísit),

content.latin: 24 Et considerémus ínvicem in provocatiónem caritátis, et bonórum óperum.
content.english: 24 And let us consider one another, to provoke unto charity and to good works:

segments.t: Et considerémus ínvicem in provocatiónem caritátis, et bonórum óperum.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Vos, qui aliquándo erátis longe, facti estis prope in sánguine Christi:
content.english: ℟. Ye, who sometimes were far off, are made nigh by the Blood of Christ.

segments.t: Vos, qui aliquándo erátis longe, facti estis prope in sánguine Christi:

content.latin: * Ipse enim est pax nostra, qui fecit útraque unum.
content.english: * For He is our Peace, Who hath made both one.

content.latin: ℣. Complácuit per eum reconciliáre ómnia in ipsum, pacíficans per sánguinem crucis eius, sive quæ in cælis sunt.
content.english: ℣. It pleased [the Father that in Him should all fulness dwell, and,] having made peace through the Blood of His Cross, by Him to reconcile all things unto Himself, [by Him, I say,] whether they be things in earth or things in heaven.

segments.t: Complácuit per eum reconciliáre ómnia in ipsum, pacíficans per sánguinem crucis eius, sive quæ in cælis sunt.

content.latin: ℟. Ipse enim est pax nostra, qui fecit útraque unum.
content.english: ℟. For He is our Peace, Who hath made both one.

segments.t: Ipse enim est pax nostra, qui fecit útraque unum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Ipse enim est pax nostra, qui fecit útraque unum.
content.english: ℟. For He is our Peace, Who hath made both one.

segments.t: Ipse enim est pax nostra, qui fecit útraque unum.

content.latin: Nocturnus II
content.english: Nocturn II

segments.t: Nocturnus II

content.latin: Ant. Pilátus, * volens pópulo satisfácere, trádidit illis Iesum flagéllis cæsum.
content.english: Ant. Pilate, * willing to content the people, delivered Jesus, when he had scourged Him, to be crucified.

segments.t: Ant.
Pilátus, * volens pópulo satisfácere, trádidit illis Iesum flagéllis cæsum.

content.latin: Psalmus 22 [4]
content.english: Psalm 22 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 22

content.latin: 22:1 Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
content.english: 22:1 The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. * He hath set me in a place of pasture.

segments.t: Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.

content.latin: 22:2 Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.
content.english: 22:2 He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: * he hath converted my soul.

segments.t: Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.

content.latin: 22:3 Dedúxit me super sémitas iustítiæ, * propter nomen suum.
content.english: 22:3 He hath led me on the paths of justice, * for his own name’s sake.

segments.t: Dedúxit me super sémitas iustítiæ, * propter nomen suum.

content.latin: 22:4 Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.
content.english: 22:4 For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, * for thou art with me.

segments.t: Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.

content.latin: 22:4 Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.
content.english: 22:4 Thy rod and thy staff, * they have comforted me.

segments.t: Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.

content.latin: 22:5 Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.
content.english: 22:5 Thou hast prepared a table before me * against them that afflict me.

segments.t: Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.

content.latin: 22:5 Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!
content.english: 22:5 Thou hast anointed my head with oil; * and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!

segments.t: Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!

content.latin: 22:6 Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
content.english: 22:6 And thy mercy will follow me * all the days of my life.

segments.t: Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:

content.latin: 22:6 Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: 22:6 And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord * unto length of days.

segments.t: Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Pilátus, volens pópulo satisfácere, trádidit illis Iesum flagéllis cæsum.
content.english: Ant. Pilate, willing to content the people, delivered Jesus, when he had scourged Him, to be crucified.

segments.t: Ant.
Pilátus, volens pópulo satisfácere, trádidit illis Iesum flagéllis cæsum.

content.latin: Ant. Videns autem * quia nihil profíceret, accépta aqua, lavit manus coram pópulo dicens: Innocens ego sum a sánguine Iusti huius.
content.english: Ant. When Pilate saw * that he could prevail nothing, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying: I am innocent of the Blood of this just Person.

segments.t: Ant.
Videns autem * quia nihil profíceret, accépta aqua, lavit manus coram pópulo dicens: Innocens ego sum a sánguine Iusti huius.

content.latin: Psalmus 29 [5]
content.english: Psalm 29 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 29

content.latin: 29:2 Exaltábo te, Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: * nec delectásti inimícos meos super me.
content.english: 29:2 I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me: * and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me.

segments.t: Exaltábo te, Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: * nec delectásti inimícos meos super me.

content.latin: 29:3 Dómine, Deus meus, clamávi ad te, * et sanásti me.
content.english: 29:3 O Lord my God, I have cried to thee, * and thou hast healed me.

segments.t: Dómine, Deus meus, clamávi ad te, * et sanásti me.

content.latin: 29:4 Dómine, eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam: * salvásti me a descendéntibus in lacum.
content.english: 29:4 Thou hast brought forth, O Lord, my soul from hell: * thou hast saved me from them that go down into the pit.

segments.t: Dómine, eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam: * salvásti me a descendéntibus in lacum.

content.latin: 29:5 Psállite Dómino, sancti eius: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis eius.
content.english: 29:5 Sing to the Lord, O ye his saints: * and give praise to the memory of his holiness.

segments.t: Psállite Dómino, sancti eius: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis eius.

content.latin: 29:6 Quóniam ira in indignatióne eius: * et vita in voluntáte eius.
content.english: 29:6 For wrath is in his indignation; * and life in his good will.

segments.t: Quóniam ira in indignatióne eius: * et vita in voluntáte eius.

content.latin: 29:6 Ad vésperum demorábitur fletus: * et ad matutínum lætítia.
content.english: 29:6 In the evening weeping shall have place, * and in the morning gladness.

content.latin: Vis sánguinis Christi audíre virtútem? Redeámus ad eius exémplum, et priórem typum recordémur, et prístinam Scriptúram narrémus. In Ægýpto, nocte média, Ægýptiis Deus plagam décimam minabátur, ut eórum primogénita deperírent, quia primogénitum eius pópulum detinébant. Sed, ne amáta plebs Iudæórum una cum illis periclitarétur, quia unus locus continébat univérsos, remédium discretiónis invéntum est. Proínde exémplum mirábile, ut discas in veritáte virtútem. Ira divínæ indignatiónis operabátur, et domos síngulas mórtifer circuíbat. Quid ígitur Móyses? Occídite, inquit, agnum annículum, et sánguine eius liníte iánuas. Quid ais, Móyses? Sanguis ovis rationálem hóminem liberáre consuévit? Valde, inquit; non eo quod sanguis est, sed quia Domínici sánguinis per eum demonstrátur exémplum.
content.english: Wouldest thou hear the power of the Blood of Christ? Then let us look at the figure thereof, let us call to mind the old type, and tell the story written in the ancient Scriptures. The Egyptians would not let God take away Israel His firstborn, And Moses said: Thus saith the Lord: About midnight will I go out into the midst of Egypt, and all the first-born in the land of Egypt shall die, from the first-born of Pharaoh that sitteth upon his throne unto the first-born of the maid-servant that is behind the mill, and all the first-born of beasts. And there shall be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there was none like it, nor shall be like it any more. But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast that ye may know how that the Lord hath put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel. Ex. xi. 4-7. Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them: Draw out and take you a lamb according to your families and kill the Passover. And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel and the two side-posts with the blood. and when He seeth the blood upon the lintel and on the two side-posts, the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you. xii. 21-23. And could the blood of a sheep save a man Yea, in good sooth not because it was blood, but because it represented in a figure the Blood of the Lord.

content.latin: Nam, sicut regnántium státuæ, quæ sine causa sunt et sermóne, nonnúmquam ad se confugiéntibus homínibus, ánima et ratióne decorátis, subveníre consuevérunt, non quia sunt ære conféctæ, sed quia rétinent imáginem principálem; ita et sanguis ille, qui irrationális fuit, ánimas habéntes hómines liberávit, non quia sanguis fuit, sed quia huius sánguinis ostendébat advéntum. Et tunc Angelus ille vastátor, cum linítos postes atque áditus pervidéret, transiécit gressus et non est ausus intráre. Nunc ergo si víderit inimícus, non póstibus impósitum sánguinem typi, sed fidélium ore lucéntem sánguinem veritátis Christi, templi póstibus dedicátum, multo magis se súbtrahet. Si enim Angelus cessit exémplo, quanto magis terrébitur inimícus, si ipsam perspéxerit veritátem? Vis et áliam huius sánguinis scrutári virtútem? Volo. Unde primum occúrrit, inspícias, et de quo fonte manávit. De ipsa primum cruce procéssit; latus illud Domínicum inítium fuit. Latus miles apéruit, et templi sancti paríetem patefécit; et ego thesáurum præclárum invéni, et fulgéntes divítias me grátulor reperíre.
content.english: The statues of monarchs, mindless and speechless images though they be, have sometimes been an helpful refuge to men endowed with soul and reason, not because they are works of the brazier's skill, but because the likeness they bear is a King's. And just so did this unconscious blood deliver the lives of men, not because it was blood, but because it foreshadowed the shedding of the Blood of Jesus. On that night in Egypt, when the destroying Angel saw the blood upon the lintel and on the two side-posts, he passed over the door, and came not in unto the house. Even so now much more will the destroyer of souls flee away when he seeth, not the lintel and the two side-posts sprinkled with the blood of a lamb, but the mouth of the faithful Christian, the living dwelling of the Holy Ghost, shining with the blood of the True Messiah. If the Angel let the type be, how shall not the enemy quail before the Reality? Wouldest thou hear more of the power of that Blood I am willing. Consider from what source it welleth, from what fountain it springeth. Its fountain is the Heart of the Lord, pierced for us upon the Cross. Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with Him but when they came to Jesus, and saw that He was dead already, they brake not His Legs, but one of the soldiers with a spear pierced His Side, and forthwith came thereout Blood and Water, John xix, 32-34, whereof One is a figure of Baptism, and the other of the Sacrament of the Altar. One of the soldiers with a spear pierced His Side and the veil of the Temple of His Body was rent in twain. John ii. 19-21, Matth. xxvii. 51. O how glorious is the treasure that is laid open to me therein! How noble the riches that it is my joy there to have found!

content.latin: Sic et de illo agno factum est: Iudǽi ovem occidérunt, et ego fructum de sacraménto cognóvi. De látere sanguis et aqua. Nolo tam fácile, audítor, tránseas tanti secréta mystérii; restat enim mihi mýstica atque secretális orátio. Dixi baptísmatis sýmbolum et mysteriórum, aquam illam et sánguinem demonstráre. Ex his enim sancta fundáta est Ecclésia per lavácri regeneratiónem, et renovatiónem Spíritus Sancti. Per baptísma, inquam, et mystéria, quæ ex látere vidéntur esse proláta. Ex látere ígitur suo Christus ædificávit Ecclésiam, sicut de látere Adam eius coniux Heva proláta est. Nam hac de causa Paulus quoque testátur dicens: De córpore eius et de óssibus eius sumus; latus vidélicet illud signíficans. Nam, sicut de illo látere Deus fecit féminam procreári, sic et de suo látere Christus aquam nobis et sánguinem dedit, unde repararétur Ecclésia. Recurrénte autem anno ab humáni géneris redemptióne undevícies centenário, quem ad tam ineffábile benefícium recoléndum solémni præ ómnibus sacro Iubilǽo summus Póntifex Pius undécimus celebrátum vóluit; ut pretiósi sánguinis quo redémpti sumus, Agni Immaculáti Christi uberióres dimanárent in hómines fructus, eiúsque memória fidélibus, vivídius commendarétur, idem summus Póntifex Pretiosíssimi Sánguinis Dómini nostri Iesu Christi festum, quotánnis ab univérsa Ecclésia peragéndum, ad ritum dúplicem primæ classis evéxit.
content.english: And so was it done concerning that Lamb: the Jews killed a sheep, and I have learned the value of the sacrament. From the Side flowed forth Blood and Water. I would not, O my hearer, that thou shouldest pass by the depths of such a mystery as this without pausing; for I have yet a mystic and mysterious discourse to deliver. I have said that the Water and Blood shewed forth symbolically baptism and the sacraments. For from these, holy Church was founded by the laver of regeneration, and the renovation of the Holy Ghost. Through baptism, I say, and through the sacraments, which seem to have issued from his Side. It was therefore out of the Side of Christ that the Church was created, just as it was out of the side of Adam that Eve was raised up to be his bride. This is the reason why Paul saith, no doubt in allusion to his Side: We are members of his Body, and of his bones. For even as God made the woman Eve out of the rib which he had taken out of the side of Adam, so hath Christ made the Church out of the Blood and Water which he made to flow for us out of his own Side. -On the occasion of the nineteenth centenary of the accomplishment of the redemption of mankind, as a fitting celebration of this ineffable blessing, Pope Pius XI decreed an extraordinary Jubilee. During that year the Supreme Pontiff, wishing that the fruits of the Precious Blood of Christ, the Lamb without spot, might redound more abundantly upon mankind and that the minds of the faithful be impressed with more vivid recollections of this same Blood as the price of their redemption, elevated the Feast of the Most Precious Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ to the rank of a double of the first class, to be celebrated as such every year by the universal Church.

segments.t: Multo ígitur magis nunc iustificáti in sánguine ipsíus, salvi érimus ab ira per ipsum.

content.latin: ℟. Quóniam cum adhuc peccatóres essémus, secúndum tempus Christus pro nobis mórtuus est.
content.english: ℟. In that, while we were yet sinners, in due time Christ died for us.

segments.t: Quóniam cum adhuc peccatóres essémus, secúndum tempus Christus pro nobis mórtuus est.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Quóniam cum adhuc peccatóres essémus, secúndum tempus Christus pro nobis mórtuus est.
content.english: ℟. In that, while we were yet sinners, in due time Christ died for us.

segments.t: Quóniam cum adhuc peccatóres essémus, secúndum tempus Christus pro nobis mórtuus est.

content.latin: Nocturnus III
content.english: Nocturn III

segments.t: Nocturnus III

content.latin: Ant. Exívit ergo Iesus * portans corónam spíneam et purpúreum vestiméntum. Et dixit eis: Ecce homo.
content.english: Ant. Then came Jesus forth, * wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate saith unto them: Behold the Man.

segments.t: Ant.
Exívit ergo Iesus * portans corónam spíneam et purpúreum vestiméntum. Et dixit eis: Ecce homo.

content.latin: Psalmus 73 [7]
content.english: Psalm 73 [7]

segments.t: Psalmus 73

content.latin: 73:1 Ut quid, Deus, repulísti in finem: * irátus est furor tuus super oves páscuæ tuæ?
content.english: 73:1 O God, why hast thou cast us off unto the end: * why is thy wrath enkindled against the sheep of thy pasture?

segments.t: Ut quid, Deus, repulísti in finem: * irátus est furor tuus super oves páscuæ tuæ?

content.latin: 73:2 Memor esto congregatiónis tuæ, * quam possedísti ab inítio.
content.english: 73:2 Remember thy congregation, * which thou hast possessed from the beginning.

segments.t: Memor esto congregatiónis tuæ, * quam possedísti ab inítio.

content.latin: 73:2 Redemísti virgam hereditátis tuæ: * mons Sion, in quo habitásti in eo.
content.english: 73:2 The sceptre of thy inheritance which thou hast redeemed: * mount Sion in which thou hast dwelt.

segments.t: Redemísti virgam hereditátis tuæ: * mons Sion, in quo habitásti in eo.

content.latin: 73:3 Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: * quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!
content.english: 73:3 Lift up thy hands against their pride unto the end; * see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.

segments.t: Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: * quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!

content.latin: 73:4 Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: * in médio solemnitátis tuæ.
content.english: 73:4 And they that hate thee have made their boasts, * in the midst of thy solemnity.

segments.t: Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: * in médio solemnitátis tuæ.

content.latin: 73:5 Posuérunt signa sua, signa: * et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.
content.english: 73:5 They have set up their ensigns for signs, * and they knew not both in the going out and on the highest top.

segments.t: Posuérunt signa sua, signa: * et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.

content.latin: 73:6 Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt iánuas eius in idípsum: * in secúri et áscia deiecérunt eam.
content.english: 73:6 As with axes in a wood of trees, they have cut down at once the gates thereof, * with axe and hatchet they have brought it down.

segments.t: Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt iánuas eius in idípsum: * in secúri et áscia deiecérunt eam.

content.latin: 73:7 Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: * in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.
content.english: 73:7 They have set fire to thy sanctuary: * they have defiled the dwelling place of thy name on the earth.

segments.t: Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: * in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.

content.latin: 73:8 Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: * Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.
content.english: 73:8 They said in their heart, the whole kindred of them together: * Let us abolish all the festival days of God from the land.

segments.t: Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: * Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.

content.latin: 73:9 Signa nostra non vídimus, iam non est prophéta: * et nos non cognóscet ámplius.
content.english: 73:9 Our signs we have not seen, there is now no prophet: * and he will know us no more.

segments.t: Signa nostra non vídimus, iam non est prophéta: * et nos non cognóscet ámplius.

content.latin: 73:10 Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: * irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?
content.english: 73:10 How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach: * is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever?

segments.t: Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: * irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?

content.latin: 73:11 Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, * de médio sinu tuo in finem?
content.english: 73:11 Why dost thou turn away thy hand: and thy right hand * out of the midst of thy bosom for ever?

segments.t: Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, * de médio sinu tuo in finem?

content.latin: 73:12 Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula: * operátus est salútem in médio terræ.
content.english: 73:12 But God is our king before ages: * he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.

segments.t: Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula: * operátus est salútem in médio terræ.

content.latin: 73:13 Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare: * contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis.
content.english: 73:13 Thou by thy strength didst make the sea firm: * thou didst crush the heads of the dragons in the waters.

segments.t: Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare: * contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis.

content.latin: 73:14 Tu confregísti cápita dracónis: * dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum.
content.english: 73:14 Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon: * thou hast given him to be meat for the people of the Ethiopians.

segments.t: Tu confregísti cápita dracónis: * dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum.

content.latin: 73:15 Tu dirupísti fontes, et torréntes: * tu siccásti flúvios Ethan.
content.english: 73:15 Thou hast broken up the fountains and the torrents: * thou hast dried up the Ethan rivers.

segments.t: Tu dirupísti fontes, et torréntes: * tu siccásti flúvios Ethan.

content.latin: 73:16 Tuus est dies, et tua est nox: * tu fabricátus es auróram et solem.
content.english: 73:16 Thine is the day, and thine is the night: * thou hast made the morning light and the sun.

segments.t: Tuus est dies, et tua est nox: * tu fabricátus es auróram et solem.

content.latin: 73:17 Tu fecísti omnes términos terræ: * æstátem et ver tu plasmásti ea.
content.english: 73:17 Thou hast made all the borders of the earth: * the summer and the spring were formed by thee.

segments.t: Tu fecísti omnes términos terræ: * æstátem et ver tu plasmásti ea.

content.latin: 73:18 Memor esto huius, inimícus improperávit Dómino: * et pópulus insípiens incitávit nomen tuum.
content.english: 73:18 Remember this, the enemy hath reproached the Lord: * and a foolish people hath provoked thy name.

segments.t: Memor esto huius, inimícus improperávit Dómino: * et pópulus insípiens incitávit nomen tuum.

content.latin: 73:19 Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi, * et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.
content.english: 73:19 Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee: * and forget not to the end the souls of thy poor.

segments.t: Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi, * et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.

content.latin: 73:20 Réspice in testaméntum tuum: * quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum.
content.english: 73:20 Have regard to thy covenant: * for they that are the obscure of the earth have been filled with dwellings of iniquity.

segments.t: Réspice in testaméntum tuum: * quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum.

content.latin: 73:21 Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus: * pauper et inops laudábunt nomen tuum.
content.english: 73:21 Let not the humble be turned away with confusion: * the poor and needy shall praise thy name.

segments.t: Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus: * pauper et inops laudábunt nomen tuum.

content.latin: 73:22 Exsúrge, Deus, iúdica causam tuam: * memor esto improperiórum tuórum, eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die.
content.english: 73:22 Arise, O God, judge thy own cause: * remember thy reproaches with which the foolish man hath reproached thee all the day.

segments.t: Exsúrge, Deus, iúdica causam tuam: * memor esto improperiórum tuórum, eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die.

content.latin: 73:23 Ne obliviscáris voces inimicórum tuórum: * supérbia eórum, qui te odérunt, ascéndit semper.
content.english: 73:23 Forget not the voices of thy enemies: * the pride of them that hate thee ascendeth continually.

segments.t: Ne obliviscáris voces inimicórum tuórum: * supérbia eórum, qui te odérunt, ascéndit semper.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Exívit ergo Iesus portans corónam spíneam et purpúreum vestiméntum. Et dixit eis: Ecce homo.
content.english: Ant. Then came Jesus forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate saith unto them: Behold the Man.

segments.t: Ant.
Exívit ergo Iesus portans corónam spíneam et purpúreum vestiméntum. Et dixit eis: Ecce homo.

content.latin: Ant. Et báiulans sibi crucem, * exívit in eum, qui dícitur Calváriæ, locum, ubi crucifixérunt eum.
content.english: Ant. And He, bearing His Cross, * went forth into a place called the place of a Skull, where they crucified Him.

segments.t: Ant.
Et báiulans sibi crucem, * exívit in eum, qui dícitur Calváriæ, locum, ubi crucifixérunt eum.

content.latin: Psalmus 87 [8]
content.english: Psalm 87 [8]

segments.t: Psalmus 87

content.latin: 87:2 Dómine, Deus salútis meæ: * in die clamávi, et nocte coram te.
content.english: 87:2 Lord, the God of my salvation: * I have cried in the day, and in the night before thee.

segments.t: Dómine, Deus salútis meæ: * in die clamávi, et nocte coram te.

content.latin: 87:3 Intret in conspéctu tuo orátio mea: * inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam:
content.english: 87:3 Let my prayer come in before thee: * incline thy ear to my petition.

segments.t: Intret in conspéctu tuo orátio mea: * inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam:

content.latin: 87:4 Quia repléta est malis ánima mea: * et vita mea inférno appropinquávit.
content.english: 87:4 For my soul is filled with evils: * and my life hath drawn nigh to hell.

segments.t: Quia repléta est malis ánima mea: * et vita mea inférno appropinquávit.

content.latin: 87:5 Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: * factus sum sicut homo sine adiutório, inter mórtuos liber.
content.english: 87:5 I am counted among them that go down to the pit: * I am become as a man without help, free among the dead.

segments.t: Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: * factus sum sicut homo sine adiutório, inter mórtuos liber.

content.latin: 87:6 Sicut vulneráti dormiéntes in sepúlcris, quorum non es memor ámplius: * et ipsi de manu tua repúlsi sunt.
content.english: 87:6 Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres, whom thou rememberest no more: * and they are cast off from thy hand.

segments.t: Sicut vulneráti dormiéntes in sepúlcris, quorum non es memor ámplius: * et ipsi de manu tua repúlsi sunt.

content.latin: 87:7 Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri: * in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.
content.english: 87:7 They have laid me in the lower pit: * in the dark places, and in the shadow of death.

segments.t: Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri: * in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.

content.latin: 87:8 Super me confirmátus est furor tuus: * et omnes fluctus tuos induxísti super me.
content.english: 87:8 Thy wrath is strong over me: * and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me.

segments.t: Super me confirmátus est furor tuus: * et omnes fluctus tuos induxísti super me.

content.latin: 87:9 Longe fecísti notos meos a me: * posuérunt me abominatiónem sibi.
content.english: 87:9 Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me: * they have set me an abomination to themselves.

segments.t: Longe fecísti notos meos a me: * posuérunt me abominatiónem sibi.

content.latin: 87:9 Tráditus sum, et non egrediébar: * óculi mei languérunt præ inópia.
content.english: 87:9 I was delivered up, and came not forth: * my eyes languished through poverty.

segments.t: Tráditus sum, et non egrediébar: * óculi mei languérunt præ inópia.

content.latin: 87:10 Clamávi ad te, Dómine, tota die: * expándi ad te manus meas.
content.english: 87:10 All the day I cried to thee, O Lord: * I stretched out my hands to thee.

segments.t: Clamávi ad te, Dómine, tota die: * expándi ad te manus meas.

content.latin: 87:11 Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: * aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?
content.english: 87:11 Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? * or shall physicians raise to life, and give praise to thee?

segments.t: Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: * aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?

content.latin: 87:12 Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, * et veritátem tuam in perditióne?
content.english: 87:12 Shall any one in the sepulchre declare thy mercy: * and thy truth in destruction?

segments.t: Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, * et veritátem tuam in perditióne?

content.latin: 87:13 Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, * et iustítia tua in terra obliviónis?
content.english: 87:13 Shall thy wonders be known in the dark; * and thy justice in the land of forgetfulness?

segments.t: Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, * et iustítia tua in terra obliviónis?

content.latin: 87:14 Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: * et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.
content.english: 87:14 But I, O Lord, have cried to thee: * and in the morning my prayer shall prevent thee.

segments.t: Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: * et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.

content.latin: 87:15 Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: * avértis fáciem tuam a me?
content.english: 87:15 Lord, why castest thou off my prayer: * why turnest thou away thy face from me?

segments.t: Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: * avértis fáciem tuam a me?

content.latin: 87:16 Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a iuventúte mea: * exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.
content.english: 87:16 I am poor, and in labours from my youth: * and being exalted have been humbled and troubled.

segments.t: Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a iuventúte mea: * exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.

content.latin: 87:17 In me transiérunt iræ tuæ: * et terróres tui conturbavérunt me.
content.english: 87:17 Thy wrath hath come upon me: * and thy terrors have troubled me.

segments.t: In me transiérunt iræ tuæ: * et terróres tui conturbavérunt me.

content.latin: 87:18 Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: * circumdedérunt me simul.
content.english: 87:18 They have come round about me like water all the day: * they have compassed me about together.

segments.t: Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: * circumdedérunt me simul.

content.latin: 87:19 Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: * et notos meos a miséria.
content.english: 87:19 Friend and neighbour thou hast put far from me: * and my acquaintance, because of misery.

segments.t: Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: * et notos meos a miséria.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Et báiulans sibi crucem, exívit in eum, qui dícitur Calváriæ, locum, ubi crucifixérunt eum.
content.english: Ant. And He, bearing His Cross, went forth into a place called the place of a Skull, where they crucified Him.

segments.t: Ant.
Et báiulans sibi crucem, exívit in eum, qui dícitur Calváriæ, locum, ubi crucifixérunt eum.

content.latin: Ant. Ut vidérunt eum iam mórtuum, * non fregérunt eius crura, sed unus mílitum láncea latus eius apéruit, et contínuo exívit sanguis et aqua.
content.english: Ant. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that He was dead already, * they brake not His legs but one of the soldiers with a spear pierced His Side, and forthwith came thereout Blood and Water.

segments.t: Ant.
Ut vidérunt eum iam mórtuum, * non fregérunt eius crura, sed unus mílitum láncea latus eius apéruit, et contínuo exívit sanguis et aqua.

content.latin: Psalmus 93 [9]
content.english: Psalm 93 [9]

segments.t: Psalmus 93

content.latin: 93:1 Deus ultiónum Dóminus: * Deus ultiónum líbere egit.
content.english: 93:1 The Lord is the God to whom revenge belongeth: * the God of revenge hath acted freely.

segments.t: Deus ultiónum Dóminus: * Deus ultiónum líbere egit.

content.latin: 93:2 Exaltáre, qui iúdicas terram: * redde retributiónem supérbis.
content.english: 93:2 Lift up thyself, thou that judgest the earth: * render a reward to the proud.

segments.t: Exaltáre, qui iúdicas terram: * redde retributiónem supérbis.

content.latin: 93:3 Úsquequo peccatóres, Dómine, * úsquequo peccatóres gloriabúntur:
content.english: 93:3 How long shall sinners, O Lord: * how long shall sinners glory?

segments.t: Úsquequo peccatóres, Dómine, * úsquequo peccatóres gloriabúntur:

content.latin: 93:4 Effabúntur, et loquéntur iniquitátem: * loquéntur omnes, qui operántur iniustítiam?
content.english: 93:4 Shall they utter, and speak iniquity: * shall all speak who work injustice?

segments.t: Effabúntur, et loquéntur iniquitátem: * loquéntur omnes, qui operántur iniustítiam?

content.latin: 93:5 Pópulum tuum, Dómine, humiliavérunt: * et hereditátem tuam vexavérunt.
content.english: 93:5 Thy people, O Lord, they have brought low: * and they have afflicted thy inheritance.

segments.t: Pópulum tuum, Dómine, humiliavérunt: * et hereditátem tuam vexavérunt.

content.latin: 93:6 Víduam, et ádvenam interfecérunt: * et pupíllos occidérunt.
content.english: 93:6 They have slain the widow and the stranger: * and they have murdered the fatherless.

segments.t: Víduam, et ádvenam interfecérunt: * et pupíllos occidérunt.

content.latin: 93:7 Et dixérunt: Non vidébit Dóminus, * nec intélleget Deus Iacob.
content.english: 93:7 And they have said: The Lord shall not see: * neither shall the God of Jacob understand.

segments.t: Et dixérunt: Non vidébit Dóminus, * nec intélleget Deus Iacob.

content.latin: 93:8 Intellégite, insipiéntes in pópulo: * et stulti, aliquándo sápite.
content.english: 93:8 Understand, ye senseless among the people: * and, you fools, be wise at last.

segments.t: Intellégite, insipiéntes in pópulo: * et stulti, aliquándo sápite.

content.latin: 93:9 Qui plantávit aurem, non áudiet? * aut qui finxit óculum, non consíderat?
content.english: 93:9 He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? * or he that formed the eye, doth he not consider?

segments.t: Qui plantávit aurem, non áudiet? * aut qui finxit óculum, non consíderat?

content.latin: 93:10 Qui córripit gentes, non árguet: * qui docet hóminem sciéntiam?
content.english: 93:10 He that chastiseth nations, shall he not rebuke: * he that teacheth man knowledge?

segments.t: Qui córripit gentes, non árguet: * qui docet hóminem sciéntiam?

content.latin: 93:11 Dóminus scit cogitatiónes hóminum, * quóniam vanæ sunt.
content.english: 93:11 The Lord knoweth the thoughts of men, * that they are vain.

segments.t: Dóminus scit cogitatiónes hóminum, * quóniam vanæ sunt.

content.latin: 93:12 Beátus homo, quem tu erudíeris, Dómine: * et de lege tua docúeris eum,
content.english: 93:12 Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord: * and shalt teach him out of thy law.

segments.t: Beátus homo, quem tu erudíeris, Dómine: * et de lege tua docúeris eum,

content.latin: 93:13 Ut mítiges ei a diébus malis: * donec fodiátur peccatóri fóvea.
content.english: 93:13 That thou mayst give him rest from the evil days: * till a pit be dug for the wicked.

segments.t: Ut mítiges ei a diébus malis: * donec fodiátur peccatóri fóvea.

content.latin: 93:14 Quia non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: * et hereditátem suam non derelínquet.
content.english: 93:14 For the Lord will not cast off his people: * neither will he forsake his own inheritance.

segments.t: Quia non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: * et hereditátem suam non derelínquet.

content.latin: 93:15 Quoadúsque iustítia convertátur in iudícium: * et qui iuxta illam omnes qui recto sunt corde.
content.english: 93:15 Until justice be turned into judgment: * and they that are near it are all the upright in heart.

segments.t: Quoadúsque iustítia convertátur in iudícium: * et qui iuxta illam omnes qui recto sunt corde.

content.latin: Vigilánti verbo Evangelísta usus est, ut non díceret: Latus eius percússit, aut vulnerávit, aut quid áliud, sed Apéruit; ut illic quodámmodo vitæ óstium panderétur, unde sacraménta Ecclésiæ manavérunt, sine quibus ad vitam, quæ vera vita est, non intrátur. Ille sanguis qui fusus est, in remissiónem fusus est peccatórum. Aqua illa salutáre témperat póculum; hæc et lavácrum præstat et potum. Hoc prænuntiábat quod Noë in látere arcæ óstium fácere iussus est, quo intrárent animália quæ non erant dilúvio peritúra, quibus præfigurabátur Ecclésia. Propter hoc prima múlier facta est de látere viri dormiéntis, et appelláta est vita matérque vivórum. Magnum quippe significávit bonum, ante magnum prævaricatiónis malum. Hic secúndus Adam, inclináto cápite, in cruce dormívit, ut inde formarétur ei coniux, quæ de látere dormiéntis efflúxit. O mors, unde mórtui revivíscunt! Quid isto sánguine múndius? Quid vúlnere isto salúbrius?
content.english: One of the soldiers with a spear pierced His Side, and forthwith came thereout Blood and Water. The Evangelist speaketh carefully. He saith not that he smote the Side, nor yet that he wounded It, nor yet anything else, but pierced It, to fling wide the entrance unto life, whence flow the Sacraments of the Church, those Sacraments without which there is no entrance unto the life which is life indeed. That Blood which was shed there was shed for the remission of sins, that Water is the water that mantleth in the cup of salvation. Therein are we washed, and thereof do we drink. Of this was it a type when it was said unto Noah: The door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof and of every living thing of all flesh shalt thou bring into the ark to keep them alive. Gen. vi. 16, 19. A figure this of the Church. Thus was it that the first woman was made from the side of her husband while he slept, and she was called (Eve, which is, being interpreted,) Life, because she was the mother of all living. Gen. iii. 20. This name set forth a great good, before it became associated with the bitter fruit of a great evil. And here we have the Second Adam bowing His Head, and the deep sleep of death falling upon Him upon the Cross, and He sleepeth, that the Lord God may take a thing out of His side, and may make thereof a wife for Him. O what a death was His, which quickeneth the dead! What is cleaner than His Blood? What more health-giving than His wounding?

content.latin: Tenebántur hómines captívi sub diábolo, et dæmónibus serviébant; sed redémpti sunt a captivitáte. Véndere enim se potuérunt, sed redímere non potuérunt. Venit Redémptor, et dedit prétium; fudit sánguinem suum, et emit orbem terrárum. Quǽritis quid émerit? Vidéte quid déderit, et inveniétis quid émerit. Sanguis Christi prétium est. Tanti quid valet? quid, nisi totus orbis? quid, nisi omnes gentes? Valde ingráti sunt prétio suo, aut multum supérbi sunt, qui dicunt, aut illud tam parum esse ut solos Afros émerit, aut se tam magnos esse pro quibus solis illud sit datum. Non ergo exsúltent, non supérbiant. Pro toto dedit, quantum dedit.
content.english: Then were being held bondsmen to the devil, slaves to evil spirits. But they have been redeemed from that bondage. They had been able to sell themselves, but they were not able to redeem themselves. A Redeemer came and paid the price for them. He shed His Blood, and at that cost bought the world. Ye ask what He bought? Look what He paid, and ye shall see what He bought. Christ's Blood was the price. What is His Blood worth? What, but the whole world? What, but all men? They are very unthankful for His redemption, or very proud, who say that It is only precious enough to buy the Africans, or that they themselves are so precious that It was shed only for them. Let there be an end to such conceit, an end to such vainglory. What He paid, He paid for all.

content.latin: Hábuit ille sánguinem, unde nos redímeret; et ad hoc accépit sánguinem, ut esset quem pro nobis rediméndis effúnderet. Sanguis Dómini tui, si vis, datus est pro te; si nolúeris esse, non est datus pro te. Forte enim dicis: Hábuit sánguinem Deus meus, quo me redímeret, sed iam, cum passus est, totum dedit; quid illi remánsit, quod det et pro me? Hoc est magnum, quia semel dedit, et pro ómnibus dedit. Sanguis Christi volénti est salus, nolénti supplícium. Quid ergo dúbitas, qui mori non vis, a secúnda pótius morte liberári? Qua liberáris, si vis tóllere crucem tuam, et sequi Dóminum; quia ille tulit suam, et quæsívit servum.
content.english: That Blood was his own, and thereby he redeemed us. Yea, it was to this end that he took Flesh and Blood, namely that he might shed his Blood in order to redeem us. If thou wilt accept it, the Blood of thy Lord was given for thee. If thou wilt not accept it, it was not given for thee. For perchance thou sayest: My God had Blood, with which he redeemed me, but now since he hath suffered, he hath given it all; what hath remained to him, that he may also give any of it for me? This is a great thing, because he gave once, and he gave for all. The Blood of Christ is salvation to him that doth accept it, punishment to him that doth not accept it. Why therefore dost thou hesitate to be set free from the second death, thou who dost not wish to die? By this thou art set free, if thou art willing to take up thy Cross, and follow the Lord; for he took up his Cross and sought his servant.
